entry.title: MCP registry and allowlist controls for Copilot in JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The MCP registry and allowlist controls for GitHub Copilot in JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode provide administrators and developers with a secure and streamlined way to manage access to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. By enabling curated discovery and installation of MCP servers from a central registry, and enforcing allowlist policies, organizations gain better oversight and control, improving security and simplifying setup across popular IDEs.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect easier setup and management of MCP server access for Copilot users in JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode IDEs. Developers will have a simple, reliable experience finding and installing approved MCP servers, while admins can enforce policies to restrict usage to only trusted servers. This reduces security risks, increases compliance, and saves time for both IT and engineering teams.

entry.title: Actions: New 1 vCPU standard hosted runner [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The new 1 vCPU / 5 GB RAM standard hosted runners for GitHub Actions provide a lightweight, cost-effective option for automation tasks, issue operations, and short-running jobs. By running workflows inside containers instead of full virtual machines, these runners make it easier and more efficient for teams to execute simple automation at scale while saving on compute resources.

Expected Outcome

Teams using these lightweight runners can expect faster startup times and reduced resource costs for smaller automation jobs. This enables organizations to run more jobs in parallel, optimize their CI/CD pipelines, and focus heavier compute resources where needed, all while lowering costs for lightweight tasks.

entry.title: Unaffiliated users for GitHub Enterprise Cloud [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Enterprise Cloud now supports unaffiliated users for all enterprises, enabling organizations to manage Copilot Business licensing and enterprise team membership independent of organization affiliation. Enterprise owners can invite users directly to the enterprise account and assign Copilot licenses without requiring organizational membership, providing greater flexibility in managing user access and licensing. This separation of enterprise membership from organization membership allows enterprises to centralize all user management under one account, whether users need access to GitHub Enterprise, Copilot, or both—streamlining administration and reducing complexity.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect more flexible and granular control over user management and Copilot licensing at the enterprise level. Enterprise administrators will be able to invite and license users for Copilot without the overhead of organization membership, making it easier to onboard contractors, external collaborators, or Copilot-only users. However, this change requires an important update to offboarding processes: users removed from all organizations will now remain as unaffiliated users in the enterprise, requiring explicit removal from the enterprise itself. Teams should audit their offboarding automation to ensure users are fully removed when needed, preventing unintended license consumption or access.

entry.title: Extended metadata checks for secret scanning [Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub secret scanning now surfaces extended metadata for leaked secrets, helping security and development teams understand ownership and impact at a glance. Beyond verifying whether a secret is active, secret scanning now displays details like the secret owner's name and email, creation and expiry dates, and organizational context for supported providers such as OpenAI, Slack, Stripe, and many others. This additional context transforms secret alerts from simple detections into actionable intelligence, enabling teams to quickly determine who owns a leaked secret, what it can access, and where it originates.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect faster triage and more effective remediation of leaked secrets. With ownership and impact information readily available, security teams can prioritize alerts more accurately, contact the right stakeholders immediately, and assess the scope of potential exposure without time-consuming manual lookups. Development teams benefit from clearer context that helps them understand the severity of each alert and take informed action. As GitHub continues to add support for additional secret types on a rolling basis, teams will gain increasingly comprehensive visibility into their secret exposure across their entire development stack.

entry.title: Assign code scanning alerts to Copilot for automated fixes [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub now enables organizations to assign code scanning alerts directly to Copilot coding agent for automated remediation. By extending Copilot's capabilities to security vulnerabilities, development teams can delegate common security fixes to Copilot, which analyzes the vulnerability, creates a remediation plan, and opens a draft pull request without manual intervention. Whether fixing alerts individually or in bulk through security campaigns, Copilot handles the heavy lifting of planning and implementing fixes, allowing developers to focus on review and innovation rather than repetitive security work.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect significantly faster vulnerability remediation cycles with reduced manual effort from both development and security teams. By automating the creation of security fixes, teams will see fewer security alerts accumulating as technical debt, faster time-to-resolution for common vulnerabilities, and more time for developers to focus on building features. Security teams gain confidence that vulnerabilities are being addressed systematically through Copilot's automated fix workflow, while maintaining full visibility and control through the pull request review process.

entry.title: Automated security and quality validation for Copilot coding agent [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot coding agent now automatically validates the security and quality of every pull request it creates. By analyzing new code using CodeQL, secret scanning, and the GitHub Advisory Database, Copilot coding agent proactively detects and resolves security vulnerabilities, sensitive information, and dependency risks. It also performs a built-in code review to catch quality issues before code is merged. This all happens seamlessly, without requiring extra configuration or a GitHub Advanced Security license, empowering teams to ship secure, high-quality code with confidence and speed.

Expected Outcome

With automated security and quality validation, organizations can expect fewer manual code review comments and security issues after Copilot coding agent creates a pull request. Teams benefit from higher-quality, more secure code shipped faster, with less effort spent on remediation and review. This update streamlines the development process and helps organizations maintain security standards while increasing productivity.

entry.title: Enable premium request and feature-level budgeting for AI tools [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub now offers dedicated premium request SKUs for Copilot Coding Agent and GitHub Spark, combined with flexible bundled budget options that give organizations crystal-clear visibility into AI tool spending. Teams can choose to manage budgets at the individual product level or through a unified approach while maintaining full cost attribution and control. This means no more guesswork about which AI tools are driving usage, and the confidence to scale AI adoption with granular spending controls.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect precise, SKU-level tracking that shows exactly how much each AI tool costs, with the ability to set budgets that match their governance needs. Enterprise and Team administrators gain enhanced policy controls to enable or disable overages per tool, while existing budgets automatically migrate to the new system without disruption. As GitHub's AI ecosystem continues to expand, this foundation ensures teams can confidently adopt new tools with transparent cost management and sophisticated AI governance built in from day one.

entry.title: Security validation tools integration with Copilot Coding Agent [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot Coding Agent now integrates security validation tools directly into its workflow, including GitHub secrets protection, CodeQL, and the GitHub Advisory Database. This means that every pull request (PR) generated by Copilot Coding Agent is automatically analyzed for potential security issues before it's finalized, giving organizations greater confidence in the safety of code changes powered by AI. By proactively incorporating leading security tools, Copilot Coding Agent helps teams avoid introducing new security risks and ensures clean, secure code delivery every time.

Expected Outcome

With security validation built into Copilot Coding Agent, organizations can expect a measurable reduction in security issues and manual remediation efforts. Teams benefit from automated code analysis and fixes, streamlined reviews, and enhanced trust in AI-generated code. This update enables organizations to ship faster while maintaining high security standards, supporting both developer productivity and peace of mind.

entry.title: Copilot coding agent integration in JetBrains IDEs
entry.content:

GitHub Copilot coding agent integration in JetBrains IDEs enables developers to delegate coding tasks directly from their JetBrains environment. By connecting Copilot agent workflows to JetBrains, developers can automate repetitive work, boost productivity, and stay focused on high-impact problems. This integration helps teams leverage AI-powered coding assistance across more of their favorite tools, making it easier to get work done without switching contexts.

With Copilot coding agent available in JetBrains IDEs, developers can expect a smoother workflow for handing off tasks to Copilot, improving task completion speed and reducing manual effort. This leads to more efficient development cycles, less context switching, and supports teams in delivering features faster. The integration ensures Copilot's benefits are accessible across even more environments, helping organizations maximize the impact of AI assistance in their daily work.

entry.title: Copilot Licensing in Enterprise for Direct user assignment & enterprise teams [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Copilot Business licensing in GitHub Enterprise enables organizations to assign Copilot licenses directly to users or teams at the enterprise level, without requiring organizational access or a GitHub Enterprise Cloud license for every user. This flexible approach centralizes license management, streamlines provisioning, and gives enterprise admins a unified view of Copilot license usage across their organization. By supporting direct user assignment and enterprise teams, this release eliminates licensing fragmentation and simplifies administration for large enterprises.

Expected Outcome

Customers can expect faster, more efficient license assignment and management for Copilot Business within their enterprise. Enterprise admins will be able to grant Copilot access to users or teams from a single, dedicated page, reducing administrative overhead and ensuring license deduplication. This enables organizations to scale Copilot adoption, provision licenses via trials, and maintain compliance with internal policies.

entry.title: Copilot coding agent on self-hosted runners [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Copilot coding agent on self-hosted runners enables organizations to run GitHub Copilot's agentic automation within their own infrastructure, giving teams control over where and how Copilot agent operates. This expands Copilot's capabilities beyond GitHub-hosted runners, allowing customers to automate coding tasks on-premises or in their preferred cloud environment—meeting security, compliance, and customization needs. Teams benefit from flexible deployment, enhanced data governance, and the ability to leverage GitHub's powerful agentic platform wherever their workflows run.

Expected Outcome

Customers can expect to accelerate delivery and reduce manual coding effort by running Copilot coding agent on self-hosted runners. Organizations gain automation and AI-powered code generation behind their own firewalls, improving operational control and scalability. This release helps teams unlock greater productivity and efficiency, while maintaining the data control, flexibility, and compliance needed for enterprise environments.

entry.title: Enterprise AI Controls & Agent Control Plane [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Enterprise AI Controls & Agent Control Plane gives GitHub Enterprise Cloud administrators centralized visibility and management over all AI and agent systems. The Agent Control Plane consolidates administrative tasks, policy management, and custom agent configuration, empowering organizations to operationalize and govern their agentic fleet from a single, intuitive interface. Customers can expect streamlined governance over AI and Copilot agents, improved auditability, and easier configuration of custom agents at scale. Enterprises gain the tools and insight needed to securely manage agent activity, enforce policy, and decentralize administration, driving trust and adoption of AI-powered automation across their teams.

GitHub Copilot coding agent empowers developers by automating repetitive and mundane coding tasks, allowing them to focus on more complex and creative work. entry.content:
Value Prop

The Copilot usage metrics dashboard and API provide GitHub Enterprise administrators and billing managers with a comprehensive view of Copilot adoption and engagement. With real-time insights into daily and weekly active users, agent adoption, code contribution trends, and language/model usage, organizations can easily understand who is using Copilot, where, and how. Enterprise customers can expect actionable, data-driven insights into Copilot usage across their organizations. entry.title: Copilot coding agent can work on existing human-created pull requests [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Copilot coding agent now helps you finish work in existing pull requests (PRs) created by humans. Just mention @copilot in a comment, and Copilot will open a new PR stacked on top of your changes, make the updates you requested, and ask for your review. You stay in control and can merge Copilot's PR into your branch when you're ready. This workflow lets you delegate repetitive or lower-priority coding tasks to Copilot, freeing you up to focus on more impactful work.

Expected Outcome

With Copilot coding agent, developers can expect to save time by letting Copilot handle parts of their coding workload in the background, even on existing branches. Teams will benefit from increased productivity, more efficient code review cycles, and the flexibility to collaborate asynchronously. This capability empowers developers to move faster, reduce manual effort, and focus on projects that matter most.

entry.title: Copilot-generated commit messages on GitHub.com [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot now suggests relevant, contextual commit messages when you add or edit files on GitHub.com. Instead of pausing your workflow to summarize your changes or settling for generic placeholders, Copilot automatically generates concise, high-quality commit messages that make your project history more meaningful and easier to understand. This saves time and helps you keep documentation consistent without extra effort.

Expected Outcome

With Copilot-generated commit messages, developers and teams can expect more consistent and informative commit histories with less manual work. This makes it easier to understand the context of changes, improves collaboration, and helps teams deliver higher-quality software faster. By reducing the friction of documentation, teams are empowered to focus on their work and ship updates with confidence.

entry.title: Grouping changes in a pull request with Copilot [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot now helps you review pull requests (PRs) more effectively by automatically grouping related changes. Instead of seeing a single list of all file changes, Copilot organizes them into logical groups—such as UI updates, backend changes, or dependency updates—so you can focus on one area at a time. This makes it easier to understand complex PRs, speeds up code reviews, and improves code quality across your projects.

Expected Outcome

With grouped changes in pull requests, developers and reviewers can expect faster, more focused code reviews. By surfacing related changes together, Copilot reduces review fatigue and helps teams catch issues earlier, leading to higher velocity and better collaboration. This feature aims to streamline the review process and make it easier to keep up with the increasing complexity of modern software development.

entry.title: Copilot Auto Model [Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot Auto Model introduces an "auto" mode that automatically selects the optimal AI model for each coding scenario. This feature removes the guesswork for users, ensuring that Copilot always delivers the best possible suggestions for their needs—whether they are writing, reviewing, or refactoring code. By streamlining model selection, Copilot Auto Model helps developers stay focused on their work, boosts productivity, and provides a seamless experience without additional configuration.

With Copilot Auto Model, customers can expect improved code quality and efficiency, as the most suitable model is chosen for their specific task in real time. This enhancement means users no longer need to manually switch models or adjust settings, reducing friction and making Copilot more intuitive. Ultimately, developers can spend more time building and less time configuring, leading to faster delivery and more reliable outcomes.

entry.content:

Custom agents for GitHub Copilot empower developers, teams, and organizations to create agent "personas" tailored to their unique workflows and needs. By defining custom configurations in a repository, users can fine-tune Copilot's behavior to enforce coding conventions, streamline automation, and optimize for specific technologies or compliance requirements without complex setup. Organizations will be able to quickly set up specialized agents to automate repetitive tasks, enforce best practices, and ensure consistent outcomes across teams. entry.title: Start and track Copilot coding agent tasks in GitHub Mobile [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Mobile now allows users to start and track Copilot coding agent tasks directly from their mobile devices. This update extends the centralized view of agent tasks experience to mobile, giving developers a seamless and consistent way to manage their Copilot coding agents on the go. By integrating Copilot agent task management into the GitHub Mobile Home view, developers are empowered to initiate, monitor, and interact with coding tasks anytime, anywhere, increasing flexibility and productivity.

Expected Outcome

With this release, developers can expect improved workflow continuity when away from their desktops. The ability to start, monitor, and manage Copilot agent tasks within GitHub Mobile means users can stay informed and take action on critical coding work, even while mobile. This helps teams remain agile, reduces bottlenecks caused by being away from a computer, and ensures that important agent-driven tasks progress efficiently across platforms.
